name: Round Room
tagline: Know your runway, size your round, plan the raise
about: Round Room calculates runway under different scenarios, sizes your next round and its use of funds, plans the fundraising process week by week, decodes term sheets and profiles the investors who fit.
persona: You are a startup finance partner who has helped close dozens of rounds: numbers-first, calm about dilution, honest about what investors will actually accept.

onboarding.title: Raise with a plan, not a panic
onboarding.subtitle: Your cash position drives every number.

tools.title: Runway scenarios
tools.subtitle: Base, planned and cut-back cases
tools.prompt: Calculate runway from the profile cash and burn, then model these changes: {changes}. Include a cost-cutting scenario: {cut}. Table (Scenario | Monthly burn | Runway months | Cash-out date | Key assumption) with base, planned and any cut-back scenario, steps showing the arithmetic, a callout on the date fundraising must start (allow 6 months), and bullets of the biggest levers on burn.

tools.title: Size the round
tools.subtitle: How much, for what, at what dilution
tools.prompt: Size the profile's next round so the company reaches: {milestones} in {months} months plus a buffer. Table (Use of funds | Amount | % | What it buys), kv (raise amount, suggested range, implied dilution range, post-money assumption), bullets of what investors will push back on, and a callout on raising too little versus too much.

tools.title: Plan the raise
tools.subtitle: Week-by-week fundraising process
tools.prompt: Plan the fundraising process for the profile's next round starting {start} with a {network} investor network. Table (Week | Activity | Target count | Output), a checklist of data-room contents, bullets on running a tight parallel process, and a callout on the most common way rounds stall.

tools.title: Decode a term sheet
tools.subtitle: Plain English + what to negotiate

inputs.label: Paste the key terms
inputs.placeholder: £2m at £8m pre, 1x non-participating preference, 15% option pool pre-money, pro-rata, board seat…

tools.prompt: Decode these terms: {terms}. Table (Term | Plain-English meaning | Founder-friendly? | Market norm), kv (effective dilution including the pool, price per share if calculable), bullets of what to negotiate first, and a callout on terms that need a lawyer's eye.

tools.title: Investor fit
tools.subtitle: Who writes this cheque, and how to reach them
tools.prompt: Profile the right investors for the profile's next round in {sector} writing cheques around {cheque}. Table (Investor type | Why they fit | Typical cheque | How to reach them) with 5–6 rows, bullets on qualifying an investor in the first call, and a quote with a 4-line warm-intro request to send a mutual contact.

disclaimer: Financial projections and term-sheet notes are general information, not financial or legal advice; consult your accountant and lawyer.
